claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Firstly, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 18 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can usually continue if they stay in approved education or training.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This typically includes:
- Full-time, non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or NVQs up to level 3)
- Certain approved training programmes

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's doing his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you! A-levels at a sixth form college counts as approved education, so that's a positive sign for your eligibility.

Now I have a few more questions:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you. 

And does Alex live with you, or do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to ensure eligibility:

Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week in paid employment, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - he does receive Universal Credit in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's an important detail.

Unfortunately, one of the rules for Child Benefit is that you'll stop receiving it if your child starts getting certain benefits in their own right, including Universal Credit.

Based on the information you've provided, I'll now provide my assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's why:**

While you meet several of the usual requirements:
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex lives with you
- ✅ Alex is under 20 and in approved education (A-levels)

Unfortunately, because **Alex receives Universal Credit in his own name**, this stops your eligibility for Child Benefit. The rules state that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts receiving certain benefits in their own right, and Universal Credit is one of those benefits.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he stops claiming Universal Credit), you may be able to make a new claim at that point.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
